title: Rupee hits eight-month high as foreign inflows lift markets; Nifty nears record peak - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
The rupee’s sharp appreciation is driven by strong FPI inflows

The rupee surged 67 paise to an eight-month high of ₹92.20 per dollar on Tuesday, buoyed by record foreign portfolio inflows, softer crude oil prices, and the Reserve Bank of India’s tolerance for currency appreciation, even as equities staged a sharp rebound from the previous session’s sell-off.

The domestic currency opened at ₹92.65 per dollar, briefly weakened to ₹92.70, before strengthening to an intraday high of ₹92.16 and settling at ₹92.20. Traders attributed the rally to sustained foreign institutional investor (FII) buying in equities, lower oil prices, and improved dollar supply conditions in the local market.

“The rupee’s sharp appreciation is driven by strong FPI inflows, softer crude oil prices and improved domestic dollar supply-demand dynamics,” said Kunal Sodhani, Head of Treasury at Shinhan Bank. “RBI’s recent forex measures have helped curb speculative positions, while increased exporter dollar selling has further supported the currency.”

The currency gains came alongside a strong recovery in equities. The BSE Sensex jumped 1,502 points, or 1.8 per cent, to close at 83,938.28, while the Nifty 50 rose 469.6 points, or 1.9 per cent, to settle at 25,819.25, recouping most of Monday’s losses and ending just 554 points away from its record high. Bank Nifty outperformed, surging 2.5 per cent to a fresh record closing high of 64,635.20.

Underlying the move was relentless foreign buying. FIIs remained net buyers, purchasing nearly ₹4,480 crore worth of equities on Wednesday and extending their buying streak to 17 consecutive sessions. Month-to-date inflows have reached about ₹1.2 lakh crore, a record monthly tally. Domestic institutional investors (DIIs) also supported the rally, buying equities worth more than ₹4,000 crore.

Hindustan Unilever led gains on the Nifty, rising more than 6 per cent, while private banks, pharma and IT stocks also advanced. Metals bucked the trend, falling around 2 per cent. Insurance stocks and distributors gained after IRDAI constituted a six-member expert committee to review proposed distribution reforms, raising expectations of softer norms and a phased implementation.

“The rebound was supported by fresh buying interest in large-cap stocks, particularly Reliance, private sector banks and FMCG companies,” said Shrikant Chouhan, Head of Equity Research at Kotak Neo. He expects 26,000 on the Nifty 50 and 84,700 on the BSE Sensex to act as near-term trigger levels, with a move above them potentially opening the door to fresh record highs.
